parts:
Dear List,

I posted some questions last week, but I didn't get an answer. I hope my=20=

seemingly long list didn't scare you off! (this list might seem quite=20
long, but a summary of the questions is given at the end). I still hope=20=

somebody can help...

<I gathered point transect data on different songbird species in differen=
t=20
forests (called =91plots=92 (strata)) in 2 seasons during 3 years.
My main aim is to compare relative densities per species in these plots.=20=

I=92m not interested in comparing densities between species, only within=20=

species between plots. Therefore, I analyse my data separately per=20
species. However, I still have some basic questions and doubts and I hope=
=20
you can help me with answering them.=20

First, I analysed densities by pooling all data per species (over years=20=

and seasons), stratifying per forest plot (detection function estimated=20=

per stratum, (1)). The histograms for some plots revealed that another bi=
n=20
grouping and truncation distance would give a better fit. Therefore, I=20=

decided to do the analyses also seperately per plot (and, of course, per=20=

species), making an individual decision for truncation and grouping for=20=

each plot and selecting the best model for each bird species per plot. I=20=

did this to test if the model, used for pooled data in the stratified=20
analysis (see (1)), was robust. Densities estimated with pooled data=20
(detection function per stratum) were very similar to the densities=20
estimated when separate analyses per species/plot were run, except for=20=

those plots where sample size was low (< 50 observations). For these=20
plots, I cannot get a good fit. My feeling is that it is then more logic=20=

to keep to the pooled data stratified per plot. Is this correct? Or shoul=
d=20
I choose 1 model, based on the smallest summed AIC=92s (sum of AIC values=
=20
per model for all plots and then choose lowest sum to decide which model=20=

is the best; as I could find as suggestion by Steven in his reply to the=20=

mail of Kristin A Bratland on 25/10/2006)?

One model (based on the pooled data) had a lower AIC value but proved to=20=

be less robust (when comparing density estimates from pooled data versus=20=

the individual plot-approach). Therefore, I intend to choose the second=20=

model or do a bootstrap analysis. I wonder if a bootstrap analysis is=20
possible with MCDS and stratification (I would enter season, as well as=20=

weather-related parameters, as covariables and stratify per forest plot)?=


I also want to compare the densities per species between plots and years.=
=20
Can I use multipliers to keep the original model, as described in the Hel=
p-
function for rare species? [note down the estimated P (detection=20
probability) and P SE (standard error) from the "Density Estimates/Global=
"=20
page of the Analysis Details Results for the analysis of the years pooled=
.=20
In the Data Explorer, create a new multiplier, and multiplier SE and ente=
r=20
the estimated P and P SE in the cells. Now, define a Data Filter that use=
s=20
the Data Selection tab to include only the year of interest. Define a=20
Model Definition that uses a Uniform key function (under Detection=20
Function Models) and 0 adjustment terms (under Detection Function=20
Adjustment Terms). Include the new multiplier and multiplier SE in this=20=

Model Definition under the Multipliers tab.]? Probably this is only=20
allowed if the =91year of interest=92 is not included in the =91global=92=
analysis=85
Another possibility would be to make unique combinations of plot+year eg=20=

plot1-2004, plot1-2005, plot1-2006; plot2-2004, plot2-2005, plot2-2006;=20=

etc and then stratify by this =91plot + year=92 parameter with a global=20=

detection function per plot. However, this will only be possible for thos=
e=20
species that are common enough to do a separate analysis per plot.


I could stratify per year and use plot as a covariable instead of=20
stratifying per plot, but this would mean I wouldn=92t get standard error=
s=20
for the plot =96 level. So is there no solution to get density estimates =
and=20
errors per species, plot and year, other than doing a separate analysis=20=

per species-plot combination and stratifying per year? Even if this=20
separate analysis would be a solution, this would only be possible for=20=

those species that are abundant enough to estimate detection functions pe=
r=20
plot.

A last question: Can I simply estimate densities per feeding guild (eg=20=

frugivores, insectivores) by hand by adding the densities of the species=20=

belonging to the same guild and calculating the variance?

Summarised, my questions are:

1.=09Is it convenient to choose different grouping cutpoints and=20
truncation levels for different strata (plots) for the same species if=20=

this seems to ameliorate the fit?
2.=09If a model with a slightly higher AIC seems to be more robust on a=20=

global scale, but for some strata the lowest AIC model is better: is the=20=

right choice to choose 1 common model based on the lowest sum of AIC-
values per model for all plots? Or is bootstrapping the better option?
3.=09Is it allowed to enter a variable (eg year) as a covariable in=20
small-sample cases, but use it for stratification in larger-sample=20
analyses? Or should the parameter =91year=92 be entered as covariable in =
all=20
cases, and is there a way to calculate the standard error in this case? I=
n=20
fact, what I need is to =91stratify=92 per plot and per year, but using a=
plot-
level detection function (if possible; for some rare species it will be a=
t=20
the global level), but this is not possible and I=92m not sure that=20
entering =91year=92 as covariate is a good option, since my aim is to gai=
n a=20
density estimate + error per plot and per year, and I don=92t expect a=20=

different detection probability per year a priori. However, I don=92t kno=
w=20
how to solve this problem.
4.=09Can I simply estimate densities per feeding guild (eg frugivores,=20=

insectivores) by hand by adding the densities of the species belonging to=
=20
the same guild and how can I then calculate the variance?



Thanks a lot for your help!

Val=E9rie Lehouck
